artiest/leon-huff.text:
Leon A. Huff was born in 1942 in Camden, New Jersey, and became the keyboardist and composer of one of the most famous songwriting and production partnerships in pop history. His partner was Kenneth Gamble of Philadelphia. They first worked together when Huff played on a recording by Candy & The Kisses in the early 1960s. In 1967 they produced their first top-five hit, Expressway to Your Heart by The Soul Survivors, and went on to write and produce for The Intruders, Archie Bell & the Drells, Wilson Pickett and Dusty Springfield, among others.

In 1971 Gamble and Huff founded Philadelphia International Records as a rival to Motown. In the 1970s the label released a string of soul hits, such as If You Don't Know Me by Now by Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes and Back Stabbers, For the Love of Money and Love Train by The O'Jays. The house studio band MFSB played on almost all of those records. The Philadelphia sound had lush strings, driving bass lines and gliding hi-hat rhythms. From it grew a new style that soon came to be called disco. In 1980 Huff also released a solo album, Here to Create Music.

The duo wrote more than three thousand songs and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2008. Their records combined sweet soul with lyrics about Black pride and social problems, forming a bridge between the soul of the 1960s and the dance floor of the 1970s.
artiest/leon-huff.listen: Listen to Love Train by The O'Jays and notice how the strings, the bass and the hi-hat combine into a driving rhythm. That is the Philadelphia sound that Gamble and Huff developed.

artiest/leon-thomas.text:
Leon Thomas was born in 1937 in East St. Louis, Illinois, and became one of the most striking singers of free jazz. He studied music at Tennessee State University and moved to New York in 1959, where he sang at the Apollo Theater and for Dakota Staton and The Jazz Messengers, among others. In 1961 he briefly joined the orchestra of Count Basie. After his military service in the army he worked with the saxophonist Pharoah Sanders. His best-known contribution from that period is The Creator Has a Master Plan from the 1969 album Karma.

In that same year his first solo record appeared on Bob Thiele's label Flying Dutchman, Spirits Known and Unknown. It was followed by 3 Shades of Blue, The Leon Thomas Album and Gold Sunrise On Magic Mountain, and in 1973 he toured with Carlos Santana's band. Thomas sang with a rich tenor and often broke out, in the middle of a song, into a yodelling, throaty technique that he called soularphone. In it, scat, soul and a search for African roots came together.

This style influenced singers such as James Moody, Tim Buckley and Bobby McFerrin. Critics called him the John Coltrane of jazz singers. He showed that the human voice in jazz could do more than melody and lyrics alone. Thomas died in New York in 1999.
artiest/leon-thomas.listen: Listen to The Creator Has a Master Plan and notice the moment when his singing turns into yodelling, almost instrumental flights. Hear how his voice sounds there like an extra instrument beside the saxophone.

artiest/leonard-bernstein.text: Leonard Bernstein (1918–1990) was a conductor, pianist and composer of both concert music and musicals. He wrote only one original film score: On the Waterfront (1954), for Elia Kazan. It opens with a lone horn, after which percussion and brass crash in. He received an Oscar nomination for it. His musicals made their way to the big screen more often. On the Town (1949) was filmed, but much of his music was replaced in the process. West Side Story (1961) stayed closer to his score, with Latin American rhythms, jazz and a tritone as a recurring motif. That film won ten Oscars and set the tone for the film musical.
artiest/leonard-bernstein.listen: Listen for the irregular rhythms, the finger snaps and the tritone (the interval of three whole tones) that keeps returning in West Side Story.

artiest/leonard-rosenman.text: Leonard Rosenman was born in New York in 1924 and studied composition with Arnold Schönberg and Roger Sessions, among others. He gave piano lessons to the young James Dean, and through Dean the director Elia Kazan asked him to score East of Eden (1955). Rosenman brought modernism to the Hollywood film. In The Cobweb (1955) he was one of the first to use twelve-tone music in a major studio film. Rebel Without a Cause (1955) has sharp dissonances and rhythms that let you hear the restlessness of young people. Later he wrote Fantastic Voyage (1966). For Stanley Kubrick's Barry Lyndon (1975) he adapted existing music by Handel and Schubert, among others, and won an Oscar.
artiest/leonard-rosenman.listen: Notice the restless, dissonant harmonies and the jolting rhythms that make the characters' inner tension audible.

artiest/leonard-slatkin.text:
Leonard Slatkin is an American conductor, author and composer, born in Los Angeles in 1944. He came from a musical family: his father Felix was a violinist and conductor, and his mother Eleanor Aller a cellist, both members of the Hollywood String Quartet. Slatkin studied in Indiana and at the Juilliard School, made his conducting debut in 1966 and became an assistant at the Saint Louis Symphony Orchestra in 1968. He returned there in 1979 as music director. Under his leadership the orchestra grew into one of the best-known in America.

With that orchestra he made many recordings for labels such as RCA and EMI. In 1985 he recorded Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker, the first complete recording of that work on CD. His discography also includes Gershwin, Ravel, Debussy, Barber and Mussorgsky. In 1984 he won a Grammy for Prokofiev's Fifth Symphony. Later he led the National Symphony Orchestra in Washington, the BBC Symphony Orchestra, the Detroit Symphony Orchestra and the Orchestre National de Lyon. In 2001 he conducted the Last Night of the Proms.

Slatkin is known for his attention to twentieth-century American and British composers. For pop listeners he is above all the man behind many classical recordings that served as a reference for decades, and his work shows how the orchestral repertoire had a market of its own in the record industry.
artiest/leonard-slatkin.listen: Listen to his recording of The Nutcracker and notice how clearly each section of the orchestra can be heard. Try to follow the flute, the strings and the percussion separately.

artiest/leonardo-garcia-alarcon.text:
Leonardo García-Alarcón is an Argentine conductor who has specialised in Baroque music. He was born in La Plata in 1976, studied harpsichord and organ, and moved to Europe in 1997. In Geneva he studied at the Centre for Early Music and became an assistant to Gabriel Garrido. In 2005 he founded his own ensemble, Cappella Mediterranea. With that ensemble he has performed at many festivals, including Ambronay. He also co-directs Ensemble Clematis with the violinist Stéphanie de Failly, and since 2010 he has been artistic director of the Chœur de chambre de Namur and La Nouvelle Ménestrandie.

His recordings have appeared mainly on Ambronay and Ricercar. They include Girolamo Frescobaldi: Il Regno D'Amore from 2009, Virtuosissima compositrice, with madrigals by Barbara Strozzi, from 2009, Handel's Judas Maccabaeus from 2010, Vespro a San Marco from 2011 and Carmina Latina from 2013. He also recorded Mozart's Requiem.

Alarcón likes to bring forgotten works back into the concert hall, such as operas and oratorios from seventeenth-century Italy. After a performance of Il diluvio universale by Michelangelo Falvetti he was awarded the honorary title of citizen of Ambronay. He teaches at the conservatoire in Geneva and researches seventeenth-century music. In this way he keeps a rich, often forgotten repertoire alive, with historical instruments and a lively, dramatic style of playing.
artiest/leonardo-garcia-alarcon.listen: Listen to a recording by Cappella Mediterranea under his direction and notice how the harpsichord or organ carries the rhythm and how the singers handle the text dramatically. Hear how alive Baroque music can sound.

artiest/leonin.text:
Léonin, also known as Leoninus, is the first known major composer of polyphonic organa. He probably worked in Paris at the cathedral of Notre-Dame and was active between about 1163 and 1190. What we know of him comes mainly from the writings of a thirteenth-century English student known as Anonymous IV. He calls him the best organist and the maker of the Magnus liber organi, the great book of organum. It was intended to enrich church services, with polyphonic settings of Gregorian chant for the gradual and the antiphonary.

In his style a soloist sings an ornate, decorated upper voice above the long notes of the Gregorian tenor chant. This produced what is known as organum purum. Later Pérotin revised the book, making it shorter and adding new sections. The music of Léonin and his school is called the Notre-Dame school and belongs to the ars antiqua. Its notes were written down in square notation.

His significance is great, even though almost everything about him is uncertain. He helped lay the foundations of Western polyphony, the idea that different voices sing independent lines at the same time. From this came the later motets, the polyphony of the Renaissance and ultimately our whole harmonic tradition. Records such as Sacred Music from 12th-century Paris bring this medieval sound back for the modern listener.
artiest/leonin.listen: Listen to a recording of Sacred Music from 12th-century Paris and notice the long-sustained low voice with an ornate, mobile upper voice above it. Try to hear how those two lines meet again and again.

artiest/leopold-mozart.text:
Leopold Mozart was born in Augsburg in 1719 and was a composer, violinist and music theorist. He is best known as the father and teacher of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. He studied in Salzburg, but was expelled from the university in 1739 for poor attendance. In 1740 he began working as a professional musician and his first publication appeared, the Trio Sonatas opus 1, the copper plates of which he engraved himself. From 1743 he played violin in the court orchestra of the prince-archbishop of Salzburg. In 1763 he became deputy Kapellmeister, and he rose no higher. In 1747 he married Anna Maria Pertl. Of their seven children only Nannerl and Wolfgang survived.

His music includes Passion cantatas, symphonies and concertos. The records in the source list include his Concertos for Trumpet, Die Bauernhochzeit, Die musikalische Schlittenfahrt and a Kindersinfonie. Whether he was really successful as a composer is disputed. The Grove Dictionary says that his works were widely circulated around 1756, but other biographers do not find him particularly remarkable.

As a teacher he was a great success. In 1756, the year Wolfgang was born, his Versuch einer gründlichen Violinschule appeared, a comprehensive textbook for the violin. It was reprinted and translated many times, and musicians still use it to learn how people played in the eighteenth century.
artiest/leopold-mozart.listen: Listen to Die musikalische Schlittenfahrt and notice the bells and the whip that depict a sleigh ride. Hear how an eighteenth-century orchestra can tell a story without words.

artiest/leopold-stokowski.text:
Leopold Stokowski was a British conductor, born in London in 1882, and one of the great names of orchestral life in the early and middle twentieth century. He studied at the Royal College of Music from the age of thirteen and worked as an organist, first in London and from 1905 at a church in New York. In 1909 he became a conductor in Cincinnati, where he introduced popular concerts and programmed works by living composers. In 1912 came the appointment at the Philadelphia Orchestra, the post with which he is most closely associated. Later he also led the NBC Symphony Orchestra, the New York Philharmonic and the Houston Symphony Orchestra, among others, and founded the All-American Youth Orchestra and the American Symphony Orchestra.

Stokowski conducted without a baton and drew a distinctive, recognisable sound from every orchestra. He was a showman who experimented with the lighting of the concert hall. He also arranged scores, above all by Johann Sebastian Bach, which critics sometimes found too free. He gave many premieres, was the only conductor to play all of Arnold Schönberg's orchestral works during the composer's lifetime, and presented Boris Godunov in America in 1929 and Wozzeck in 1931. His records include Peter and the Wolf from 1941 and Carmina Burana from 1959.

For pop listeners he is best known for Disney's Fantasia, for which he conducted the music and in which he appeared on screen himself. In this way he brought classical music to the cinema and to a new audience. He gave his last public performance in 1975 and died in 1977.
artiest/leopold-stokowski.listen: Listen to the music of Walt Disney's Fantasia and notice how the orchestra changes its tone with every turn of the music. Can you hear how the mood can go from friendly to menacing?

artiest/leopold-stokowski-en-the-philade.text:
Leopold Stokowski was a British conductor, born in London in 1882 and died in 1977. He studied at the Royal College of Music, first worked as an organist in New York and in 1909 became conductor of the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra. In 1912 he became head of the Philadelphia Orchestra. He stayed there for a long time, and his name is tied to that orchestra. He also led many other orchestras and founded several himself.

Stokowski was known as a showman. He conducted without a baton, sometimes threw the score on the floor to show that he did not need it, and experimented with light in the concert hall. He also altered the orchestration of works, for example by Bach, Beethoven and Tchaikovsky. This drew criticism, but his orchestral arrangements of Bach are famous. He also played a great deal of new music and gave numerous premieres.

His best-known film work is Disney's Fantasia from 1940, for which he conducted the music. It includes The Sorcerer's Apprentice. In this way he brought classical music to the general public and let the orchestra be heard in the cinema, far beyond the concert hall. He gave concerts until 1975 and made recordings until shortly before his death.
artiest/leopold-stokowski-en-the-philade.listen: Listen to The Sorcerer's Apprentice and notice how the orchestra suggests image and action with short motifs and changing tone colours. Which instruments do you hear most?

artiest/leroy-jenkins.text:
Leroy Jenkins was an American violinist, violist and composer, born in Chicago in 1932. He grew up among records by Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie and Billy Eckstine and was given a violin as a child. At school he played clarinet and alto saxophone, because there was no orchestra. Later he studied in Florida. In the mid-1960s he returned to Chicago, where he joined the circle of the AACM, the collective of experimental jazz musicians. There he played in a trio with Anthony Braxton and Leo Smith, which recorded 3 Compositions of New Jazz in 1968. In 1969 the trio moved to Paris.

In 1970 Jenkins left for New York. He founded the Revolutionary Ensemble with the bassist Sirone and the drummer Jerome Cooper, a group that lasted about six years. He also played and recorded with Alice Coltrane, Don Cherry, Carla Bley and Rahsaan Roland Kirk. Records under his own name include For Players Only in 1975 and The Legend of Ai Glatson in 1978. In the 1980s he led the group Sting, with two violins, two guitars, electric bass and drums.

Jenkins was one of the few violinists in free jazz and showed that the instrument could have a raw voice of its own there. Later he wrote mainly for the theatre and the concert hall: the jazz-rap opera Fresh Faust, the cantata The Negro Burial Ground and the opera The Three Willies. He died in New York in 2007.
artiest/leroy-jenkins.listen: Listen to For Players Only and notice how the violin can sing, scrape and tear, sometimes within a few seconds. Try to hear how he improvises with the other players.

artiest/les-arts-florissants.text:
Les Arts Florissants is a French Baroque ensemble founded in 1979 by the American-French harpsichordist and conductor William Christie. The name comes from the 1685 opera Les Arts florissants by Marc-Antoine Charpentier. The group consists of a small vocal ensemble and an orchestra that plays on historical instruments. Its home base is the theatre in Caen, and today the ensemble is also affiliated with the Philharmonie de Paris.

The ensemble became best known for Baroque opera. The great breakthrough came in 1987 with Lully's Atys, which firmly established Christie and his group as Baroque specialists. Recordings such as Pastorale, Purcell: Dido and Aeneas from 1986 and Petits motets from 1987 had already appeared. Later came Charpentier's Médée in 1993, among others, and many rarely performed works. The recordings appeared mainly on Harmonia Mundi and Erato. Besides opera, the ensemble performs oratorios, cantatas, madrigals, masses and motets.

The ensemble plays with a clear, light sound and pays close attention to text and drama. Many former members became leading conductors of early music themselves, such as Marc Minkowski, Christophe Rousset and Hugo Reyne. In this way Les Arts Florissants shaped a large part of the French rediscovery of the Baroque.
artiest/les-arts-florissants.listen: Listen to Atys and notice how the singers declaim the French text and how the orchestra, with harpsichord and strings, follows their line. Try to hear where the music accompanies a dance or a stage scene.

artiest/les-arts-florissants-en-paul-agn.text:
Les Arts Florissants is a French Baroque ensemble, founded in 1979 by the conductor William Christie. The name comes from Marc-Antoine Charpentier's 1685 opera Les Arts florissants. The ensemble consists of a chamber orchestra on historical instruments and a small vocal ensemble. Christie is still artistic director. Since 2020 the British tenor Paul Agnew has been his co-director. The ensemble is based at the Philharmonie de Paris and has a home base in Caen.

The group has had its greatest success with Baroque operas, both on stage and in concert form. International fame came around the turn of 1986 into 1987 with a production of an opera by Lully. In 1993 followed Charpentier's Médée. The ensemble also performs oratorios, cantatas, madrigals, masses and motets, the forms of early music. Many recordings appeared on Harmonia Mundi and Erato. Sometimes it also plays contemporary music, such as the world premiere of a work by Betsy Jolas in 1999.

Many former members became well-known conductors of early music themselves, such as Marc Minkowski, Christophe Rousset, Hugo Reyne and Hervé Niquet. They founded ensembles of their own. In this way Les Arts Florissants had a great influence on the revival of early music, in which musicians play with the instruments and playing styles of the period itself. Monteverdi's madrigal Cruda Amarilli from 1605 fits that repertoire.
artiest/les-arts-florissants-en-paul-agn.listen: Listen to Cruda Amarilli and notice how the voices take over from one another and how the harmony grates at certain words. Try to hear when all the voices sing together and when they sing apart.

artiest/les-mccann.text:
Leslie Coleman McCann was born in 1935 in Lexington, Kentucky, into a family in which most of the children sang in church choirs. As a boy he played tuba and drums and taught himself piano for the most part. During his time in the navy he won a singing contest, which took him to The Ed Sullivan Show. He then moved to California and started a trio of his own. He turned down an offer to play with Cannonball Adderley because he wanted to make his own music. In the early 1960s he recorded with his trio for Pacific Jazz, including Jazz Waltz and McCann / Wilson.

His breakthrough came in 1969 with Swiss Movement, a live record with the saxophonist Eddie Harris and the trumpeter Benny Bailey, recorded at the Montreux Jazz Festival. It contains the protest song Compared to What, which reached the pop charts together with the album. After that McCann put more emphasis on his singing and became an innovator of soul jazz, in which jazz, funk, soul and world rhythms came together. He used electric piano, clavinet and synthesizer. In 1971 he took part in Ghana in a fourteen-hour concert for more than a hundred thousand people, which was captured in the film Soul to Soul.

After a stroke in the 1990s he returned in 2002 with Pump it Up. He kept releasing music until 2018 and was also a painter and photographer. His recordings have been widely sampled in hip-hop. McCann died in 2023.
artiest/les-mccann.listen: Listen to Compared to What and notice the driving piano riff and the fierce, almost spoken singing. Note that this is a live recording: can you hear the audience joining in?

artiest/les-mccann-en-eddie-harris.text:
Les McCann was an American jazz pianist and singer, born in 1935 in Lexington, Kentucky. He grew up in a musical family, played tuba and drums as a boy and taught himself piano for the most part. During his military service in the navy he won a singing contest and appeared on The Ed Sullivan Show. He then started a trio of his own in California and recorded for Pacific Jazz in the early 1960s.

In 1969 the album Swiss Movement was released on Atlantic, recorded at the Montreux Jazz Festival with the saxophonist Eddie Harris and the trumpeter Benny Bailey. It contains Compared to What, a protest song against the war in Vietnam, written by Eugene McDaniels. McCann had already recorded it as a ballad in 1966. Both the song and the album reached the American pop charts. In 1971 McCann and Harris took part in a concert in Accra, captured in the film Soul to Soul.

After Swiss Movement McCann put more emphasis on his singing. He was regarded as an innovator of soul jazz, in which jazz meets funk, soul and world rhythms. He used electric piano, clavinet and synthesizer. His recordings have been sampled in hip-hop by almost three hundred artists. McCann died in 2023.
artiest/les-mccann-en-eddie-harris.listen: Listen to Compared to What and notice the tight, driving piano riff and the direct singing. Can you hear the audience joining in?

artiest/les-paul.text:
Les Paul's real name was Lester Polsfuss. He was born in 1915 in Waukesha, Wisconsin. As a child he played harmonica, piano, banjo and guitar, and at thirteen he was already performing as a country singer. Even then he had started to tinker: to make his acoustic guitar louder, he fixed a record-player needle to the guitar and connected it to a radio loudspeaker. In Chicago he played country music on the radio by day under the name Rhubarb Red, and jazz as Les Paul in the evening. He admired Django Reinhardt, and with Bing Crosby he had a number 1 hit in 1945.

In 1940 he built The Log, one of the first electric guitars with a solid body: a block of wood with a pickup and strings, to which, for the look of it, he attached two halves of a hollow guitar. A solid guitar gave less feedback and let notes sustain longer. Gibson was not interested at first, but in 1952 put the Gibson Les Paul on the market, based on his designs. That guitar later became one of the most important instruments of rock.

At least as important were his studio inventions. In his garage in Hollywood he recorded parts on top of one another, first on acetate discs and from 1949 on an Ampex tape recorder. On Lover (When You're Near Me) he played eight guitar parts, some of them recorded at half speed. With his wife, the singer Mary Ford, he made records in the 1950s on which her voice sounded in many layers. In this way he laid the foundation for multitrack recording and for effects such as tape delay. He died in 2009.
artiest/les-paul.listen: Listen to How High the Moon by Les Paul and Mary Ford and notice Ford's voice: it sounds like a whole choir, because she recorded herself over and over. Hear, too, how Les Paul's guitar plays fast, high runs that sound almost mechanical.

artiest/les-percussions-de-strasbourg.text:
Les Percussions de Strasbourg is the oldest still-active French percussion ensemble for contemporary classical music. It grew out of an ad hoc group of six percussionists who played Le Visage Nuptial by Pierre Boulez in Strasbourg in 1959. In 1962 the ensemble was officially founded by the percussionist Jean Batigne, and on 17 January of that year it gave its first concert for French radio. In 1967 the six musicians performed Ionisation by Edgard Varèse, a piece that normally requires thirteen percussionists.

The group recorded extensively and commissioned hundreds of new pieces. The records of the 1960s and 1970s contain works by Serocki, Silvestrov, Amy and Haubenstock-Ramati, among others. On two occasions the ensemble worked with the Greek composer Iannis Xenakis: Persephassa in 1969, in which the audience sits inside a circle of musicians, and Pléiades in 1979. They also contributed to the film music for La Guerre du Feu from 1981, composed by Philippe Sarde. The percussionist Pierre Moerlen, later known from the rock band Gong, was a member in the 1970s.

The line-up remained stable for a long time and was later expanded into a larger group with a changing membership. The ensemble showed that percussion is not merely accompaniment but a sound world of its own, with many sounds, rhythms and spatial effects. That fitted well with the composers who explored the limits of music in the postwar era.
artiest/les-percussions-de-strasbourg.listen: Listen to Persephassa by Xenakis and notice how the sounds move through the space. Try to hear how the six players pass the strokes to one another.

artiest/les-siecles.text:
Les Siècles is a French symphony orchestra founded in 2003 by the conductor François-Xavier Roth. The orchestra aims to put music from the seventeenth to the twenty-first century in a new light. For that reason it plays every repertoire on the historical instruments that belong to the year of its composition. Berlioz or Bizet thus sound on instruments from their own time, and Debussy or Stravinsky on different ones again. The orchestra performs regularly in Paris, including at the Opéra Comique and the Philharmonie, but also in Amsterdam, London, Cologne and Tokyo.

In 2013 the publisher Boosey & Hawkes exceptionally gave the orchestra permission to play The Rite of Spring as it sounded on 29 May 1913 at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées. That performance was recorded, together with Petrushka in the 1911 version. The Stravinsky album won the Edison Classical Award in the Netherlands and the Preis der deutschen Schallplattenkritik in 2012. Other recordings are Symphonie fantastique from 2010, the pairing of Bizet and Chabrier from 2007, and records with Debussy and Saint-Saëns.

The musicians also teach and perform in schools, hospitals and prisons. The orchestra shows that a symphony can sound different when the instruments are the old ones, and thereby makes clear that performance practice is not the exclusive preserve of the Baroque.
artiest/les-siecles.listen: Listen to Symphonie fantastique and notice the tone colour of the woodwinds and brass, which sound different from those on modern instruments. Look for the moments where the wind instruments stand out most.

artiest/les-six.text:
Les Six is the name of a group of six composers, five Frenchmen and a Swiss, who lived and worked in Montparnasse in Paris. The name comes from two articles that the critic and composer Henri Collet wrote in Comœdia in 1920. The members were Georges Auric, Louis Durey, Arthur Honegger, Darius Milhaud, Francis Poulenc and Germaine Tailleferre. Their music is often seen as a neoclassical reaction to both Wagner and Impressionism.

The group grew out of the concerts that the writer Blaise Cendrars and the painter Moïse Kisling organised in 1917, when many theatres were closed because of the war. Milhaud later said that Collet chose the six names completely arbitrarily, because the composers knew one another and appeared on the same programmes. Poulenc said that their music was too different for a shared aesthetic: Honegger aligned himself with German Romanticism, Auric and Poulenc followed Jean Cocteau, and they disagreed about Satie, whom Auric, Milhaud and Poulenc admired. Cocteau was eager to become the leader of a musical avant-garde. Together they frequented the bar Le Bœuf sur le toit, named after Milhaud's ballet. The collaborative work Les mariés de la tour Eiffel comes from this circle.

The group never remained a bloc, but its name stands for a Parisian atmosphere of playful, clear and sometimes ironic music between the world wars. In that circle classical composers mingled with cabaret, jazz and variété.
artiest/les-six.listen: Listen to Les mariés de la tour Eiffel and notice the rapid shifts of style and mood. Try to hear where the music imitates a little dance, a march or a café song.

artiest/leslie-bricusse.text:
Leslie Bricusse was a British composer, lyricist and playwright, born in Southfields, London, in 1931. He studied at Cambridge, where he performed with the Footlights and wrote for student theatre. In the 1960s and 1970s he worked a great deal with Anthony Newley. Together they wrote the musical Stop the World – I Want to Get Off, which yielded the Grammy-winning What Kind of Fool Am I?, and The Roar of the Greasepaint – The Smell of the Crowd. As a lyricist he also worked with Cyril Ornadel, Henry Mancini and John Williams.

Bricusse wrote the music and lyrics for the films Doctor Dolittle from 1967, Goodbye, Mr. Chips from 1969, Scrooge from 1970 and Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory. He won an Oscar for Talk to the Animals. Sammy Davis Jr. had hits with What Kind of Fool Am I? and The Candy Man. Nina Simone sang his Feeling Good, Shirley Bassey made Goldfinger a worldwide success and Nancy Sinatra sang You Only Live Twice. In 1989 he was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame.

His songs have survived many styles, from musical theatre to soul and jazz, because the melodies are strong and the lyrics direct. In 2015 his memoirs, Pure Imagination, appeared, with a foreword by Elton John. Bricusse died in 2021.
artiest/leslie-bricusse.listen: Listen to Feeling Good in the version by Nina Simone and notice how the a cappella opening turns into an orchestra with brass. Can you hear how a stage song becomes a soul classic?

artiest/leslie-cheung.text:
Leslie Cheung was born in 1956 in Kowloon, then British Hong Kong, and died in 2003. He was a singer, songwriter and actor and is regarded as one of the founders of Cantopop, Cantonese pop music. As a boy he studied in England and he returned in 1976. In 1977 he took part in a singing contest and was afterwards offered contracts as an actor and recording artist. His first records were not a success.

The breakthrough came with The Wind Blows On in 1983, a cover of a Japanese song, and in 1984 with Monica, also a Japanese cover. In 1986 he starred in John Woo's action film A Better Tomorrow. He became famous throughout Asia. In 1987 Summer Romance appeared, one of the best-selling albums in Hong Kong. In 1989 he announced his retirement from music. As an actor he appeared in Days of Being Wild, 霸王别姬 (Farewell My Concubine) and Happy Together.

In 1995 he returned with Most Beloved. On the 1996 album Red he worked with the composer C. Y. Kong and the lyricist Lin Xi on a bolder sound, with experiments and a deliberately ambiguous self-image. His music ranged from cheerful dance music to sensitive ballads. He became a symbol for the Chinese-speaking world.
artiest/leslie-cheung.listen: Listen to 當年情 and notice the way the melody and the voice together create a warm, slightly wistful mood. Which instruments support the singing?

artiest/lester-bowie.text: The trumpeter Lester Bowie grew up in St. Louis and named Louis Armstrong as his first example. He played in blues bands and came to Chicago in 1966, where he became a member of the AACM and of the Art Ensemble of Chicago. On stage he wore a white doctor's coat. His playing was full of humour, with smears, growls and quotations from pop music, but also with the warmth of old jazz. As early as The Great Pretender (1981) he played pop songs; from 1984 he did so with Brass Fantasy as well, a group of nine brass players and drums. He was also often heard in the Netherlands. He died in 1999.
artiest/lester-bowie.listen: Notice the humour in the trumpet: slides, growls and sudden silences.

artiest/lester-flatt.text:
Lester Flatt was an American singer, guitarist and mandolin player and one of the pioneers of bluegrass. He was born in 1914 in Duncan's Chapel, in Overton County, Tennessee. At twelve he left school to work in a textile mill. In 1939 his career began on the radio. In 1943 he played mandolin and sang in The Kentucky Pardners, Charlie Monroe's band, and in 1945 Charlie's younger brother Bill Monroe brought him into his Blue Grass Boys.

In 1948 Flatt and the banjo player Earl Scruggs left Monroe's band and started a group of their own, Flatt and Scruggs and the Foggy Mountain Boys. For twenty years they were one of the most successful bands in bluegrass. They reached a large audience with The Ballad of Jed Clampett, the theme music of the television series The Beverly Hillbillies in the early 1960s. In 1969 Flatt and Scruggs split up. Flatt founded The Nashville Grass, with most of the members of the Foggy Mountain Boys, and made records with them such as Flatt Out (1970). He died in Nashville in 1979.

Flatt played rhythm guitar with thumb and forefinger, a style he had partly picked up from Charlie Monroe. While Scruggs drew attention with his fast banjo, Flatt provided the foundation with his firm rhythm and full singing voice. Together they defined how traditional bluegrass sounds. In 1985 they were inducted together into the Country Music Hall of Fame.
artiest/lester-flatt.listen: Listen to Foggy Mountain Breakdown by Flatt and Scruggs and first notice Earl Scruggs's lightning-fast banjo. Then listen again and focus on Lester Flatt's guitar underneath: it keeps the tempo tight and gives the song its drive.

artiest/lester-young.text: Lester Young played the tenor saxophone differently from Coleman Hawkins: with a light, airy tone and melodies that float across the bar lines. He named the saxophonist Frankie Trumbauer as his example. In 1936 he made his first recordings with a small group from Count Basie's band, in which he was the great soloist until 1940. He recorded a series of records with Billie Holiday; she gave him the nickname 'Prez', and he called her 'Lady Day'. In 1944 he was drafted into the army, where he was severely punished. His cool, relaxed way of playing became a model for Cool Jazz.
artiest/lester-young.listen: Hear how the saxophone plays lightly and unhurriedly across the beat.

artiest/leszek-mozdzer.text: The pianist Leszek Możdżer was born in Gdańsk in 1971 and received a classical training at the music academy of his city. From 1991 he played in the group Miłość, which in the 1990s also performed and recorded with the trumpeter Lester Bowie. He became known for his own arrangements of Chopin and for solo records such as Piano (2004). With the Swedish bassist Lars Danielsson and the Israeli percussionist Zohar Fresco he recorded The Time in 2005; they have played together as a trio ever since. On the album Komeda (2011) he plays the music of Krzysztof Komeda solo. His playing combines classical technique with jazz improvisation.
artiest/leszek-mozdzer.listen: Listen to the clear, classical touch, while the music is freely improvised.

artiest/lew-tabackin.text:
Lew Tabackin is an American jazz saxophonist and flautist, born in Philadelphia in 1940. He began on flute at twelve and on tenor saxophone at fifteen. As a saxophonist he named Al Cohn and Coleman Hawkins as examples; on flute he chose classical players such as Jean-Pierre Rampal. He studied flute at the Philadelphia Conservatory of Music. In 1967 he met the pianist Toshiko Akiyoshi when he was playing in Clark Terry's band. They formed a quartet in the late 1960s and married in 1969.

In 1973 they founded a big band together in Los Angeles, the Toshiko Akiyoshi Lew Tabackin Big Band, which later continued as the Toshiko Akiyoshi Jazz Orchestra. Records under his own name include Let The Tape Roll in 1975, Tenor Gladness and Trackin' in 1977, Rites of Pan in 1979, My Old Flame in 1983 and Angelica in 1985. He also recorded with Phil Woods.

The critic Scott Yanow calls him one of the few jazz musicians who have developed two completely different personalities on two instruments: a powerful hard bop style on saxophone and a delicate style on flute. Outside his music he supports the Jazz Foundation of America, which helps older jazz and blues musicians. In the history of the big band he is an important soloist in an orchestra that linked Japanese and American jazz.
artiest/lew-tabackin.listen: Listen to a recording on which Tabackin plays both tenor saxophone and flute, for example Rites of Pan. Notice the difference between the sturdy, rough saxophone and the light, singing flute.

artiest/lewie-steinberg.text:
Lewie Polk Steinberg was born in 1933 in Memphis, Tennessee, into a Baptist family. He played bass guitar and is known as the first bassist of the soul band Booker T. & the M.G.'s. He joined the group in 1962. He can be heard on Green Onions and on its B-side Behave Yourself, and on the albums Green Onions and Soul Dressing. Green Onions became the group's best-known song.

In 1965 Steinberg left the band. His place was taken by Donald Duck Dunn, who in the following years gave the group a distinctive, recognisable bass line of its own. Steinberg therefore remained known mainly for the group's first years, but his contribution to those early recordings was essential. The bass held the rhythm firmly and calmly, while organ and guitar took the melody.

In 1992 Steinberg was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Booker T. & the M.G.'s. In 2007 he received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. He died in Memphis in 2016, aged 82. He shows how much a bassist can add to an instrumental song, even without a solo or vocals.
artiest/lewie-steinberg.listen: Listen to Green Onions and notice the repeating bass line beneath the organ. Hear how the bass pushes the song forward without ever drawing attention to itself.

artiest/liam-gallagher.text:
Liam Gallagher is an English singer, born in Manchester in 1972, the youngest son of Irish immigrants. He grew up in the Burnage district and shared a bedroom with his older brother Noel. As a boy he cared more about sport than music, but as a teenager he fell under the spell of The Beatles, above all John Lennon, and of The Stone Roses, The Kinks, The Jam and T. Rex. A Stone Roses concert in 1988 changed his life, according to him. He never set foot inside an art school; he got a few qualifications at school and worked for a time at the tax office.

In 1991 he became the singer of the Manchester band The Rain, which soon became Oasis. Noel joined as guitarist and songwriter. In 1993 the group signed to Creation Records. The debut Definitely Maybe (1994) became the fastest-selling debut album in British history, and (What's the Story) Morning Glory? (1995) became one of the best-selling British albums ever. Be Here Now (1997) sold more than 400,000 copies on its first day. Together with Blur, Oasis became the face of Britpop, and the rivalry between the two bands filled the newspapers. In 2009 Oasis broke up after a quarrel between the brothers. Liam carried on with Beady Eye and later as a solo artist, with As You Were (2017), among others.

Gallagher is known for his nasal voice with drawn-out vowels, his stance at the microphone and his big mouth. He sang Noel's songs with a swagger that made Oasis a band of their own for many working-class young people.
artiest/liam-gallagher.listen: Listen to Live Forever by Oasis and notice Liam Gallagher's voice: nasal, with long drawn-out vowels at the end of the lines. Hear how he rises above the wall of guitars without ever shouting.

artiest/liberation-music-orchestra.text:
The Liberation Music Orchestra is a large jazz ensemble that the bassist Charlie Haden founded in 1969, the first band under his own leadership. The arrangements were by the pianist Carla Bley. Haden started the group at the height of the war in Vietnam, out of frustration that the government put so much energy into that war and so little into problems at home. The music was experimental and explored both free jazz and political music. The first album dealt with music from the Spanish Civil War, which had greatly inspired Haden.

The original line-up included Gato Barbieri, Dewey Redman, Paul Motian, Don Cherry, Andrew Cyrille, Roswell Rudd and Howard Johnson, among others. With the orchestra Haden wanted to let the voices of oppressed peoples be heard and to show solidarity with progressive movements around the world. In 1982 The Ballad of the Fallen appeared on ECM, which again dealt with the Spanish Civil War and with the American role in Latin America. The group toured extensively in the 1980s and 1990s. In 1990 it returned with Dream Keeper, and in 2005 Haden brought it together with new members for Not In Our Name, which dealt with American politics of that moment. In 2016 Time/Life appeared.

The orchestra showed that jazz could be a vehicle for political protest, without the music becoming a slogan. In this way it became a model for later politically engaged jazz projects.
artiest/liberation-music-orchestra.listen: Listen to a recording of Dream Keeper and notice how the large brass section plays together and how soloists break away from it. Can you hear how Haden's bass carries everything?

artiest/lifetime.text:
Lifetime is an American band from New Brunswick, New Jersey, that played melodic hardcore and emo. The group formed in 1990 around the singer Ari Katz and the guitarist Dan Yemin, with roots in the hardcore scene of New York and New Jersey. Katz wrote his lyrics in a more positive and personal vein than the negative, sometimes violent tone that many New York hardcore bands chose. That gave the group a character of its own in a tough scene.

The first album, Background, appeared in 1993 and still bore little resemblance to the later, more melodic work. In 1995 stability arrived with the guitarist Pete Martin, the bassist David Palaitis and the drummer Scott Golley. That year the second album, Hello Bastards, appeared on Jade Tree Records. In 1996 came a compilation of singles and unreleased songs, and in 1997 the third album, Jersey's Best Dancers: twelve songs in less than twenty-four minutes. Shortly afterwards the band stopped.

After the split the members carried on in other punk bands, such as Kid Dynamite and Paint It Black. In 2005 Lifetime played three reunion shows, after the festival Hellfest had been cancelled, and in November the band announced that it was really coming back. In 2007 a new album appeared, Lifetime. Hardcore with vocals that anyone can sing along to, fast guitars and honest lyrics became an important example for later emo and pop-punk bands.
artiest/lifetime.listen: Listen to Hello Bastards and notice the furious tempo and the vocals that almost scream yet still follow a melody. Can you hear how short and direct the songs are?

artiest/lil-hardin-armstrong.text: Lil Hardin grew up in Memphis, studied music at Fisk University and moved to Chicago, where she demonstrated sheet music in a music shop. She became the pianist in King Oliver's Creole Jazz Band and in 1924 married Louis Armstrong. She encouraged him to leave Oliver and build a career of his own, and played piano on the recordings of the Hot Five. She wrote pieces such as Struttin' with Some Barbecue and My Heart. After their divorce she led bands of her own, including in the 1930s for Decca. She kept playing in Chicago all her life and died in 1971 on stage, during a memorial concert for Armstrong.
artiest/lil-hardin-armstrong.listen: Notice the piano in the rhythm section: solid, right on the beat, the foundation beneath the horns.

artiest/lil-jon.text:
Lil Jon, real name Jonathan H. Smith, is an American rapper and producer, born in Atlanta in 1971. He is regarded as one of the founders of crunk, a club-oriented form of hip-hop. At fifteen he taught himself to DJ and played at house parties in his parents' basement. Later he worked as a DJ in clubs in downtown Atlanta, where he met Jermaine Dupri. Dupri hired him as an A&R at his label So So Def Recordings, where he started the compilation series So So Def Bass All-Stars.

With his group Lil Jon & the East Side Boyz and as a producer he defined the sound of the early 2000s. He produced hits such as Salt Shaker by Ying Yang Twins, Freek-a-Leek by Petey Pablo, Goodies by Ciara and Yeah! by Usher. The last of these earned him a Grammy. In 2010 his album Crunk Rock appeared. In 2013 came Turn Down for What, an EDM single with DJ Snake that won a Billboard Music Award for top dance/electronic song.

What marks Lil Jon is his raw, shouting voice, often used as a cue or ad-lib, which gives every song a party character. His production, with hard synthesizers and stomping beats, brought southern club culture to the pop charts and brought hip-hop and dance music closer together.
artiest/lil-jon.listen: Listen to Yeah! by Usher and notice the short, sharp synthesizer line and Lil Jon's shouts between the verses. Can you hear how those beats keep the song on the dance floor?

artiest/lil-jon-en-the-east-side-boyz.text:
Lil Jon & The East Side Boyz is an American hip-hop group from the southern United States, associated with crunk, a style of southern hip-hop. The early albums, such as Get Crunk, Who U Wit from 1997 and Put Yo Hood Up from 2001, were already attracting attention in their home region. The album Kings of Crunk appeared in 2002 and became the showpiece of the style. Certified Crunk followed in 2003 and Crunk Juice in 2004.

The breakthrough came in 2003 with the single Get Low, featuring the duo Ying Yang Twins as guests. The song was already on Kings of Crunk. Get Low reached number two on the American Billboard Hot 100 and entered the top ten in the United Kingdom. It was regarded as the song that brought crunk to a wide audience. Several edited radio versions appeared, because the lyrics contain a great deal of strong language.

The music is made for the dance floor. Lil Jon also worked on Yeah! by Usher from 2004, in which a line from Get Low returns. Get Low has been used in films and computer games and still turns up at parties and in series. In this way the group showed that regional club music from the South could reach a wide audience.
artiest/lil-jon-en-the-east-side-boyz.listen: Listen to Get Low and notice the voices of Lil Jon and the guests. Notice the rhythm, too.

artiest/lil-kleine.text:
Lil Kleine, real name Jorik Scholten, is a Dutch rapper, actor and singer, born in Amsterdam in 1994. He grew up in De Wallen and later in Amsterdam-Oost. He was on the books of talent agencies at a young age and made his debut in 2005 in the film Diep. After a friendship with the rapper Lange Frans he performed with his band D-Men. In 2012 he adopted the name Lil' Kleine and released his first EP, Tuig van de Richel.

In 2013 he signed to the hip-hop label TopNotch and made the single Drank & Drugs with Ronnie Flex, which reached number one in the Single Top 100 and won the 3FM Award for best single in 2016. In February 2016 his debut album Wop! appeared. In the first week all eleven tracks were in the top 35 of the Single Top 100 and the album reached number one. It was the first Dutch hip-hop album to manage that. Alleen followed in 2017, Jongen van de straat in 2020, KLEINE in 2021 and Ibiza Stories in 2022.

Lil Kleine showed that Dutch-language rap can reach a wide audience, above all through streaming. His songs mix street stories with melodic choruses and a club atmosphere. He also appeared on Expeditie Robinson and was a coach on The Voice of Holland.
artiest/lil-kleine.listen: Listen to Drank & Drugs and notice the melodic chorus and how the two voices of Lil Kleine and Ronnie Flex alternate. Can you hear how the beat stays calm while the lyrics are fierce?

artiest/lil-nas-x.text:
Lil Nas X's real name is Montero Lamar Hill and he was born in 1999 in Atlanta, Georgia. As a teenager he mostly kept to himself, and much of his time went on the internet. He made comedy clips and memes and learned how to make something go viral on Twitter. After a year of computer science at university he dropped out to make music. He worked in a fast-food restaurant and an amusement park, wrote and recorded songs in his closet and chose his name as a tribute to the rapper Nas.

In December 2018 he released Old Town Road, a blend of country and rap. He had bought the beat anonymously for thirty dollars on a website, from the Dutch producer YoungKio. That beat uses a sample from Nine Inch Nails. He recorded the song in less than an hour in a cheap studio in Atlanta. He then promoted it himself with memes, until it was picked up on TikTok, where thousands of users made their own clips to it. Old Town Road spent nineteen weeks at number 1 in the United States, a record at the time.

In the same period he announced that he is gay, the first artist with a number 1 hit to his name to do so. The EP 7 (2019) followed, and the album Montero (2021), with Montero (Call Me by Your Name) and Industry Baby. Lil Nas X is the example of a new route to the top: without a record company, with a laptop, social media and an audience that does the promotion itself.
artiest/lil-nas-x.listen: Listen to Old Town Road and notice how two worlds come together: the lyrics about horses and cowboys from country, and the heavy bass and hi-hats of trap from hip-hop. Can you hear the banjo in the beat?

artiest/lil-reese.text:
Lil Reese, real name Tavares Lamont Taylor, is an American rapper from the drill scene of Chicago. He was born in 1993 and grew up in the Englewood neighbourhood on the city's South Side, in a large family. His childhood was spent in a notorious high-rise complex, the Calumet Buildings, where he joined a gang at a young age. That milieu forms the background of drill, a hard, dark style of hip-hop from Chicago.

His name became known through his guest appearance on I Don't Like by Chief Keef in 2012, which reached the Billboard Hot 100. The music videos Us and Beef followed. The producer No I.D., who had earlier worked on records by Common and Kanye West, noticed him. That led to a record contract. His debut mixtape Don't Like appeared in 2012. A remix of Us with Rick Ross and Drake appeared on Rick Ross's The Black Bar Mitzvah. He also worked with producers such as Young Chop. Later three EPs appeared, and the album Demon Time from 2022.

His contribution to pop history lies in the wave of drill music that came out of Chicago around 2012 and that linked the southern trap sound with raw, direct stories about street life. His calm, gritty voice became a recognisable feature of that scene.
artiest/lil-reese.listen: Listen to I Don't Like by Chief Keef and notice Lil Reese's verse, with his raw voice and short phrases. Can you hear how the slow, hard beat underneath sets the menacing atmosphere?

artiest/lil-wayne.text:
Lil Wayne, real name Dwayne Michael Carter Jr., is an American rapper, singer, songwriter and label boss, born in New Orleans in 1982. He grew up in the Hollygrove neighbourhood and wrote his first rap at the age of eight. In 1993 he was discovered by Birdman, co-founder of Cash Money Records, who became his mentor. In 1997 he formed the group Hot Boys with B.G., Juvenile and Turk.

His solo debut, Tha Block Is Hot from 1999, was an immediate success. Lights Out followed in 2000 and 500 Degreez in 2002. With Tha Carter in 2004 and Tha Carter II in 2005 he kept growing. He is seen as the man who reinvented the mixtape world in the 2000s. Tha Carter III from 2008 became his biggest record. In 2010 Rebirth appeared, with which he tried to blend rap and rock and which received bad reviews. That year he served an eight-month prison sentence for weapons possession, and his album I Am Not a Human Being appeared during that time.

The source calls him one of the most influential hip-hop artists of his generation. He won five Grammys and sold more than 120 million records worldwide. His style is marked by the raw, hoarse voice, the quick punchlines and the way he lets a free, associative stream of rhymes be heard.
artiest/lil-wayne.listen: Listen to a track from Tha Carter III and notice the wordplay and Wayne's hoarse voice. Try to hear how he rhymes on unexpected words.

artiest/lili-boulanger.text: Lili Boulanger grew up in a Parisian family of musicians and was the younger sister of Nadia Boulanger, later a renowned teacher of composition. In 1913, with her cantata Faust et Hélène, she became the first woman to win the Prix de Rome for composition. She was ill all her life and died in 1918, at the age of twenty-four. In that short time she wrote music with a dark colour of its own, such as the great psalm setting Du fond de l'abîme.
artiest/lili-boulanger.listen: Listen to the beginning of Du fond de l'abîme and hear how low, heavy instruments build up a dark sound before the choir enters.

artiest/linda-mccartney.text:
Linda McCartney was born Linda Eastman in 1941 in Scarsdale, in the state of New York. Her father was an entertainment lawyer. She herself chose photography. She began in the mid-1960s at the magazine Town & Country, where she soon received assignments to photograph musicians. By the end of that decade she was a regular at the New York concert hall Fillmore East, where she worked as house photographer. She was the first woman to have a photograph on the cover of the magazine Rolling Stone, and her photographs later hung in the Victoria and Albert Museum, among other places.

After the break-up of the Beatles in 1970 she made the album RAM together with her husband Paul McCartney. She had learned to play keyboards from him. In 1971 they founded the band Wings, in which she played keyboards and sang harmonies. She continued to perform with Paul until 1993, even after Wings broke up in 1981. In 1998, after her death, the album Wide Prairie appeared.

Linda McCartney was also active for animal rights. She wrote vegetarian cookbooks, and together with her husband she started the company Linda McCartney Foods. In the course she appears as a photographer: the photo of Hendrix with a group of children on the Alice in Wonderland statue in Central Park is by her. It shows that with her camera she stood close to the music, before she played in it herself. She died in 1998.
artiest/linda-mccartney.listen: Listen to a track from RAM, the album she made with Paul. Notice the harmony vocals she sings alongside his voice.

artiest/linda-ronstadt.text:
Linda Ronstadt was born in 1946 in Tucson, Arizona, into a family of Mexican and German descent in which a great deal of music was made. She grew up with Mexican songs, rock 'n' roll, rhythm and blues, gospel and country, all styles that she would later record. In 1964 she moved to Los Angeles, where she formed the folk-rock group The Stone Poneys with Bobby Kimmel and Kenny Edwards. As a solo artist she released Hand Sown… Home Grown in 1969, which has been described as the first alternative country record by a female artist. Her backing band on Linda Ronstadt from 1971 consisted of musicians who would later form the Eagles.

The breakthrough came with Heart Like a Wheel in 1974, followed by Simple Dreams in 1977 and Living in the USA in 1978. With these she became the first female rock star to fill arenas and the most popular female singer of the 1970s. Her only number one on the Billboard Hot 100 was You're No Good. In the 1980s she appeared on Broadway in The Pirates of Penzance, receiving a Tony nomination for it, recorded traditional pop standards with the conductor Nelson Riddle and made an album of Mexican songs, Canciones de Mi Padre. She also sang duets with James Ingram and Aaron Neville.

Ronstadt gave songs by other writers a new life and managed to perform them with a powerful, clear voice, in many genres. She won eleven Grammys. After 2000 she noticed her voice deteriorating, and in 2011 she stopped singing.
artiest/linda-ronstadt.listen: Listen to You're No Good and notice how her powerful voice rises above the band without straining. Can you hear how she brings a country song and a rock song together?
